item1.justification: The trace correctly applies element-by-element anticipation analysis under §102 for claims 10/17-19 and uses Graham/KSR factors (scope and content, differences, PHOSITA level, secondary considerations) for the §103 obviousness analysis of claims 11-16, invoking the right statutory framework throughout.

item2.justification: Each rejection is linked to specific prior art (US-2013101804-A1 and US-2012268412-A1) with citations to particular disclosures (e.g., elevations E, recesses R, skin layer, user interface applications) and specific claim language (e.g., UV-curing coating material, parallel extensions, finger-guiding haptics).

item3.justification: The §102 novelty findings (claim 10 not novel, claims 11-16 novel) are consistently carried forward into the §103 stage (claim 10 obvious under single reference, claims 11-16 obvious over Schneider plus general knowledge), and the final decision mirrors these conclusions without contradiction.

item4.justification: With strictness of 0.603 (moderately strict) and combination_threshold of 0.566 (moderate), the examiner issues rejections on all claims but relies on 'common general knowledge' for several §103 combinations—a moderate but not overly permissive approach—which is consistent with the profile dimensions without being either unusually lenient or unreasonably strict.

item5.justification: The final decision to reject all claims directly follows the accumulated stage analyses: §102 rejection of claim 10 from novelty stage, §103 rejections of claims 11-16 from obviousness stage, and §102 rejection of claims 17-19 from novelty stage, with the summary restating the same rationale.
